JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation due to death of Kumara C in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners is as follows:-
That on 27-01-2024 at about 6-15 pm., Kumara C was riding his Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-51-HD-3168 from Bellur cross side towards Kunigal side.

When he reached near Magadipalya circle, (Koppa Gate on the left side of NH -75, at that time the driver of Tractor with Trailer bearing Chassis No.T052656090GM, Engine No.E-2648900, Trailer Reg.No.KA-44-T-6691 came from Kunigal side in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly took tractor towards Koppa side without any indicators or signal and dashed to the motorcycle, result of which Kumar C fell down along with his bike and sustained fatal injuries.

Immediately, Kumar C was shifted to CHC, Kunigal wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to A.C Giri Renuka G vs Krishna B T on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77221066/
2 Hospital, wherein taken initial treatment he was advised for higher hospital for further more management

entities.text: A.C Giri Renuka G vs Krishna B T
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , Kumar C was shifted to Shreyas Hospital, Bengaluru in another hire vehicle by paying Rs.5,000/-, wherein duty doctors attended and confirmed the death of C Kumar as brought dead.
3. Prior to the accident, Kumar C was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 52 years.

He was working as Lab technician at Government Hospital, Madduru and was getting monthly salary of Rs.45,000/-
per month and was having agriculture income upto Rs.3,00,000/- per annum.
Due to the untimely death of Kumar C, petitioners are put to great mental shock and agony.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1, 3 and 4 have remained absent.
Hence they are placed ex-parte.

5. Respondent no.2/ the insurer of Tractor with Trailer bearing Chassis No.T052656090GM, Engine No.E-2648900, Trailer Reg.No.KA-44-T-6691 has filed written statement and contended that Tractor with Trailer bearing Chassis No.T052656090GM, Engine No.E-2648900, Trailer Reg.No.KA-44-T-6691 was not involved in the accident, the petitioners in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gains and that the driver of the Tractor with Trailer was not holding valid driving license.
It is further contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself without observing the traffic rules.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased Kumar C succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 27-01-2024 at about 6-15 pm., near Magadipalya Circle, Koppa Gate, on NH- 75 road, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tractor with Trailer bearing Chassis No.T052656090GM, Engine No.E- 2648900, Trailer Reg.No.KA-44-T-6691 ?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for Compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3
. What order or Award ?
7. The petitioner No.2 got examined himself as Pw1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.

The respondent no.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioners have categorically contended that on 27-01-2024 at about 6-15 pm.,
when Kumara C (hereinafter called the deceased) was riding his Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-51-HD-3168 from Bellur cross side towards Kunigal side and when he reached near Magadipalya circle, (Koppa Gate on the left side of NH -75, at that time the driver of Tractor with Trailer bearing Chassis No.T052656090GM, Engine No.E- 2648900, Trailer Reg.No.KA-44-T-6691 (hereinafter referred as to the offending the vehicle) came from Kunigal side in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly took tractor towards Koppa side without any indicators or signal and dashed to the motorcycle, result of which Kumar C fell down along with his bike and sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the hospital.
11.

In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.2 who is the son of deceased got examined himself as Pw1 and produced in all 11 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P7 i.e., F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, seizure mahazarin Inquest mahazar, IMV report, etc., are the material documents to prove the present issue.
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Prasad C K, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 0008/2024 of Amruthur Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 304-A of IPC.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 304-A of IPC.
13.

The respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the fact of accused/Anand was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident and submitted that based on the information provided by the eye witness to the accident Mr. B T Krishna was driving the offending vehicle and despite of the statement, charge sheet was filed against Mr. Anand.

It is further submitted that the FIR which is the initial document prepared by the police based on the complaint or information received about a cognizable offence sets the foundation for the investigation and even though eye witnesses attributes the cause of accident by B T Krishna but charge sheet was filed against Mr. Anand and thereby Mr.
Anand has been falsely implicated in the case in the place of original accused hence submitted to dismiss the claim petition.
14.

In the light of the argument canvassed to the aforesaid effect by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2, if the materials placed on record is perused, as per the case of petitioners, one Nagaraj who has been examined as PW.2 is an eye witness to the accident.
In the charge sheet also PW.2 and one Tejas has been cited as an eye witness.
Complainant is the son of the deceased and based on the information given by the eye witness regarding the accident, the complainant has lodged the complaint.
The complaint is lodged after two days of the accident.

In the complaint and in the FIR, reason for delay in lodging the complaint has been explained stating that after shifting Renuka G vs Krishna B T on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77221066/
4 the dead body to the hospital, the complainant has lodged the compliant.

sentences.text: From the documents placed on record it can be gathered that soon after the accident the deceased was shifted to the hospital and at Shreyas Hospital he was declared brought dead.
It is quite natural that when member of the family met with an accident and succumbed to the injuries, the family members will be in grief.
Hence, delay in lodging the complaint is satisfactorily explained.
15. If the averments of the complaint is perused, wherein the vehicle involved in the accident is mentioned as "Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-44-T- 6691".
Nowhere in the complaint the name of the driver of the offending vehicle is mentioned either as B T Krishna or as Mr. Anand.
It is not in dispute that B T Krishna is the owner of the offending vehicle and he is arrayed as respondent no.1.
In none of the police documents including spot mahazar, B T Krishna is shown as the driver of the offending vehicle.
Even in para no.10 of the FIR the name of the driver of the offending vehicle is not mentioned.

In spite of that in the FIR at column 6, having mentioned at the first instance that the name of the driver of the offending vehicle as "Not known" further mentioned the name Krishna B T as the driver of the offending vehicle.

As borne out by documents, charge sheet was filed against Mr.
Anand as the driver of the offending vehicle.

It is not made known, on what basis in the FIR at column 6 the name B T Krishna is shown as the driver of the offending vehicle when there is no mention in the complaint of the name of B T Krishna as the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is true that the PW.1 has deposed that on the basis of the information given by PW.2 regarding the accident he has lodged complaint.
The PW.2 has also stated that he has stated the name of the driver of the offending vehicle to the complainant.
The PW.2 nowhere has stated that B T Krishna was the driver of the offending vehicle.
Even the complainant either in his evidence or in his complaint at Ex.P1 has stated that B T Krishna was the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further no single suggestion was posed either to the PW.1 or to the PW.2 by the respondent no.2 that at the time of accident B T Krishna was the driver and Mr. Anand was falsely implicated in the case.
Further it is nowhere the case of the respondent no.2 that since B T Krishna was not holding valid driving license, driver was shifted from B T Krishna to Mr.Anand.

The respondent no.2 having disputed Mr.Anand as the driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident and categorically contended that B T Krishna was the driver, but to substantiate the said contention, they have not taken any pain to examine the investigating officer.
Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves that Anand was the driver of the offending vehicle but not B T Krishna.

16. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, as per the case of petitioners, at the time of accident deceased was proceeding from Yediyur towards Kunigal on the left side of the road, at that time the offending vehicle which came from Kunigal side in order to go towards Koppa gate side, took the vehicle towards right turn without giving any signal or putting indicator and dashed to the motorcycle.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the deceased was proceeding on the extreme left side of Yediyur - Kunigal road.
The offending vehicle which came from Kunigal side took the vehicle towards right turn and hit to the motorcycle.
Hence the topography of the scene of occurrence one reflected in the spot sketch clearly reveals that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
When the driver of the offending vehicle was taking right turn he had to take the turn by giving signal and by confirming that no vehicle is moving at the place where he is taking right turn.
Hence, without discussing much on this point, this court holds above issue in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue no 2 :
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners, it can be said that deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
It is stated that at the time of accident deceased was aged about 52 years.
In this regard, petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased as per Ex.P8 which reflects the date of birth of deceased as 18-07- 1971.
As the accident in question has taken place in the year 2024, it can be said that deceased was aged about 53 years as on the date of accident.

18. It is contended by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner no.2 being the son and petitioner No.3 and 4 being the parents of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.
19. As per the evidence of PW.1 who is the petitioner no.2, he is aged about 26 years and being Civil Engineer in diploma he is working in RK company drawing monthly salary of Rs.18,000/-.
Hence, it can be said that petitioner no.2 though is the legal representative of the deceased but not the dependent of the deceased.
The petitioner no.1 being the wife and petitioner no.3 and 4 being the parents of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.

20. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was working as lab technician at Government Hospital, Madduru and was getting monthly salary of Rs.45,000/ per month and also having agriculture income upto Rs.3,00,000/- per annum.

The petitioners have produced Bank statement of the deceased at Ex.P11 and examined District T B Elimination Officer at Mandya as PW.3 and got marked ID card and salary slips as per Ex.P12 and Ex.P13.
From the evidence of PW.3 and from the documents it can be gathered that from 2006 the deceased was working as lab technician on contract basis.

As per Ex.P13 ie., salary slip the last drawn gross salary of the deceased in the month of January -2024 was Rs.32,282/- and after deducting professional Tax of Rs.200/-, his net salary was Rs.32,082/-.

Hence, the monthly income of the deceased is considered as Rs.32,082/-.
21.

Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, son parents and they are stated to have resided together with the deceased, but the petitioner no.2 is major son he is not dependent on the deceased

, 1/3rd of the annual income is to be deducted towards he personal expenses and remaining 2/3rd is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
22.

Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

Hence in the instant case as the victim was 53 years the addition towards future prospect should be 10%.

sentences.text: Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.32,082/-, by adding 10% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.35,290/-, out of it if 1/3rd is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.23,527/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 51 to 55 is '11'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.31,05,564/-
(Rs.23,527/- x 11 x 12 =Rs.31,05,564/-).

24. Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 has lost her husband, petitioner no.2 has lost his father and Petitioner No.3 and 4 have lost their son in their old age, thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned, slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate,
loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

25. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
26.

In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
2 Transportation and funeral Rs. 18,150/-
expenses 3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs. 1,93,600/-
parental consortium (Rs.48,400X4) 4 Loss of Dependency Rs. 31,05,564/-
Total Rs
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.33,35,464/- and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.

The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.3 :- In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 & 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners are hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.33,35,464/- + cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No. V & VI.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.33,36,464/- (Rupees Thirty Three Lakhs Thirty Six Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Four only).
A Sum of Rs.33,35,464/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the amount with interest within 2 months from the date of award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs. 26,88,064/-

Petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs. 48,400/- Petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs. 3,00,000/-
Petitioner No.4 is entitled for Rs. 3,00,000/-

Out of the amount, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1, 3 and 4 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50%
shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification through E- payment.
So far as the amount apportioned to the petitioner no 2 is concerned same is ordered to be released in his favour after due identification through E -payment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

parental consortium and filial consortium.
